response.rationale: R4 is the only candidate consistent with the raw data: acetaminophen exposure, high anion gap metabolic acidosis with normal lactate, ketones, and salicylate, and risk factors (malnutrition, renal impairment, sepsis) strongly suggest pyroglutamic acidemia. R1 is contradicted by normal lactate; R2 by low salicylate; R3 by low ketones; R5 by unchanged renal function and high anion gap (RTA typically normal anion gap).

rejected.why: Lactic acidosis is ruled out by normal lactate (0.7 mmol/L).
Salicylate toxicity is ruled out by low salicylate (<0.4 mmol/L).
Diabetic ketoacidosis is ruled out by low blood ketones (<0.2 mmol/L).
Renal tubular acidosis is contradicted by unchanged renal function and high anion gap (RTA usually normal anion gap).
